Yes — a portable power station can work as a UPS (uninterruptible power supply) for your computer, but only if it supports automatic power switchover and switches quickly enough to prevent your computer from shutting down. Not every power station can do this reliably.

What to look for

Transfer time: Prefer a documented 10 ms switchover for a computer that may be sensitive to brief power interruptions. Even 10 ms is not guaranteed to work with every PC.

UPS/EPS mode: Confirm the manufacturer explicitly supports backup operation while the station is connected to wall power.

Power output: Make sure the station can handle your computer's normal power draw and any startup peaks.

Battery capacity: More watt-hours (Wh) generally means longer runtime.

Pure sine wave output and pass-through support: Verify these are supported for your intended setup.

Sources: Anker's UPS guidance, EcoFlow's UPS guidance.

When a dedicated UPS is better

Choose a traditional UPS instead if your computer must not experience a power interruption, you need voltage regulation or surge protection specifically designed for computer equipment, or you cannot confirm that your power station's transfer time is acceptable. For servers and other critical equipment, an online double-conversion UPS is the safer choice when zero transfer interruption is required.

One important caveat: The supplied results do not establish that any of the listed power stations will keep every computer running through an outage. Confirm the exact model's UPS behavior and your computer's power-supply requirements before relying on it.
